summary: Authors may use generative AI responsibly for tasks like idea generation, copyediting, translation, literature classification and coding help, but must verify outputs and disclose the tool, version, how and why it was used. AI cannot be an author, and AI may not be used to create or manipulate research results or diagnostic images. Editors and reviewers must never upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools; reviewers may only use AI to improve review language, and editors should check with their T&F contact before using any tool.

evidence.quote: Taylor & Francis supports the responsible use of Generative AI tools that respect high standards of data security, confidentiality, and copyright protection
Authors must clearly acknowledge within the article or book any use of Generative AI tools
Generative AI tools must not be listed as an author
does permit use of Generative AI tools to assist research data visualisations and conceptual illustrations of processes, flow diagrams or teaching illustrations.
Generative AI may be utilised to assist with improving review language.
peer reviewers must not upload unpublished manuscripts or project proposals, including any associated files, images, or information, into Generative AI tools.
Editors should check with their Taylor & Francis contact prior to using any Generative AI tools
